description:
We’re Team Atlas from Bangladesh. We’re interested in robotics, coding, and using data to solve local problems. For our Field Shift project, we built a soil-sensing prototype and a crop rotation planner that uses NASA climate data to help farmers decide what to plant next.

Learn more about us at teamatlasbd.net.
summary:
We built Field Shift to help farmers decide what to plant next. Our soil probe collects field readings, and our app uses ten years of NASA POWER temperature and rainfall data alongside local soil information, crop traits, and irrigation access to compare crop rotations. In our demo, the app suggests mungbean, followed by Aman rice and lentil, for a field with limited irrigation. Field Shift helps farmers plan across seasons and explore rotations that make better use of available water and support soil health.

To learn more about Field Shift and see Team Atlas’s prototype, demo video, and project materials, visit our Google Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BSkOTGkgtw11-VXchRy6ekUDmtgmzoA-?usp=sharing

To learn more about Team Atlas, visit https://www.teamatlasbd.net/
details:
We built Field Shift, a crop rotation planner that helps farmers decide what to plant next and what to grow after that. We paired a standalone ESP32 soil probe prototype with an app that uses ten years of NASA POWER temperature and rainfall records near Dhaka, from 2015 to 2024. The moisture probe samples the soil, and a DHT sensor reads air temperature and humidity. The app also shows how farmers could enter soil report values such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and pH.

The planner checks planting windows, crop duration, soil texture, and irrigation access. It ranks the rotations that fit using historical climate patterns and farmer priorities, such as conserving water or including more legumes. In our demo, limited irrigation rules out the Boro rice rotation. The planner explains the result and puts mungbean → Aman rice → lentil first for the example field.

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the app, Arduino C++ for the ESP32 firmware, and OpenSCAD for concept modeling. Our design brings regional climate history, field readings, and farmer priorities into one view. By showing the reasons behind each ranking, Field Shift helps farmers plan across seasons, work within their water limits, and explore rotations that could support soil health.

To know more about the project visit:

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_vsesxbSCuv8w7PKpAQHWTLOt_NEm5kK?usp=sharing
